clue.text: Damn traitor is reinstated as functionary

indicators.note: reinstated read as put back together in a new order, so the three words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A treacherous official has been put back in post after a scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is reinstated' looks like the traitor's fate, but 'reinstated' is the anagram signal working on DAMN TRAITOR IS, with 'is' doing double duty only in the surface; the fodder is all thirteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A functionary is an official who carries out duties, which is exactly what an administrator does.

clue.text: Cleaner put off a chap

parts.note: to put someone off is to deter them
a gent is a chap, a man

explanation.surface: Someone who cleans for a living has discouraged a certain man.
explanation.definitionFit: Detergent is a cleansing agent, a substance used for washing.

clue.text: Useless in two school subjects in short?

parts.note: taken as written
abbreviations of two school subjects: E for English and PT for physical training
abbreviations of two school subjects: E for English and PT for physical training

explanation.surface: A pupil is hopeless at a couple of classes, in brief.
explanation.walkthrough: The two subjects are abbreviated: E (English) and PT (physical training, the old name for school PE).
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means lacking skill, so clumsy and ineffective.

clue.text: Elementary form is nothing to sophisticated poet

parts.note: O, the round figure zero, stands for nothing

indicators.note: sophisticated in its old sense of adulterated or altered, so the letters of poet are reworked

explanation.surface: A simple form of verse means nothing to a worldly poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sophisticated' rearranges POET into TOPE; 'to' is a link. 'Elementary' points to chemical elements, not simplicity.
explanation.definitionFit: An isotope is one variety of a chemical element, differing in its neutron count.

clue.text: Altered faulty foot control

indicators.note: something faulty is wrong, so the letters of the first word are put in a different order

explanation.surface: A pedal for the foot has been modified and now does not work properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faulty' rearranges the letters of 'Altered'.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadle is a lever worked by the foot to drive a machine, as on an old sewing machine.

clue.text: You can't stop them being awfully good facts

indicators.note: awfully means badly, so the letters of good facts are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Uncontrollable things are, oddly, terribly good facts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' rearranges GOOD FACTS; 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Acts of God are natural disasters such as floods and earthquakes, events no human can prevent.

clue.text: It's picked from tree with hesitation

parts.note: the oak is a tree
um is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: Something gathered from a tree, with a moment of pause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked from tree' suggests fruit, but the definition is just 'It's picked': oakum is loose fibre picked from old ropes, a task once given to prisoners; 'from' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Oakum was made by picking apart old tarred rope, a punishment chore in workhouses and prisons.

clue.text: Conservative girl has to resist element of Marxist analysis

parts.note: lass is a girl
to struggle is to resist or fight against

explanation.surface: A Tory young woman must oppose a key part of Marxist thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: In Marxist theory history is driven by conflict between social classes, the central idea of that analysis.

clue.text: Not able to bring the news?

definitions.text: Not able to bring the news?

parts.words: Not able to bring the news?
parts.note: intelligence can mean news or information, so someone without it cannot bring any; the everyday sense is simply dim-witted

explanation.surface: A messenger who fails to deliver the latest reports.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads 'not able' as lacking brains, then reinterprets intelligence as military or secret news.
explanation.definitionFit: A person lacking intelligence is dull, but read literally they lack information, news to pass on.

clue.text: Put spotlight on man not all supple

parts.note: to light something up is to put a spotlight on it, giving lit
he is a pronoun for a man
some means part, not all

explanation.surface: A stage instruction: illuminate a performer, though not the whole cast, who is agile.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are LIT, HE and SOME in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithesome is a variant of lissom, meaning flexible and graceful in movement.

clue.text: Sign of approval when getting into double figures, just

indicators.note: getting into means the approval letters are placed inside the number

parts.note: ten is the smallest number in double figures, so just reaching them
OK signals approval

explanation.surface: A gesture of assent once a cricketer's score has just reached ten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' and 'when' are links; TEN is 'just' double figures because it is the first two-digit number.
explanation.definitionFit: A token is a sign or symbol, as in a token of esteem.

clue.text: Walk on street's familiar path

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street
a rut is a habitual, well-worn track or routine

explanation.surface: Strolling along a road on the route one always takes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To strut is to walk in a stiff, swaggering way.

clue.text: Unusual, patient person on island is a casual worker

parts.note: odd means unusual
Job in the Bible is the model of patience
the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A strange, long-suffering islander takes casual work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' and 'is a' are links. The patience of Job is proverbial; the Isle of Man lies between Britain and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: An odd-job man is a handyman hired for occasional small tasks, so irregular work.

clue.text: There's power in strong material used on English church feature

indicators.note: in means the power letter goes inside the strong material

parts.note: steel is a strong material
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: A building note: reinforced metal is used on an English church's tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'There's' and 'used on' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A steeple is the tall tower and spire on a church.

clue.text: Take sandwich at repast a bit at a time

parts.note: in Scotland and northern England a piece is a sandwich or snack
a repast is a meal

explanation.surface: Eating a sandwich at mealtime, nibbling gradually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take' and 'at' are links. 'Piece' for a sandwich is Scottish and northern English usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Piecemeal means done gradually, in stages rather than all at once.

clue.text: Freshly agreed about ing

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Freshly agreed about ing (2,5)' is cut short: the wordplay needs a word giving N inside the anagram of AGREED, and the definition is missing ('ing' is a fragment); no source found.

clue.text: Getting programme for after wedding?

definitions.meaning: picking up a broadcast on radio or television is its ...
the party held after a marriage ceremony

explanation.surface: Tuning in to a show to watch after the marriage service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' links the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Reception is both the receiving of a broadcast signal and the formal party following a wedding.

clue.text: About to have a party,

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'About to have a party, (7)' is cut short after the comma: RE (about) and TREAT (party) give the wordplay but the definition is missing; no source found.

clue.text: Queen in transport which will cover this?

definitions.text: Queen in transport which will cover this?

indicators.note: in means the royal letters are placed inside the vehicle word

parts.note: a train is a form of transport
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: The monarch rides a vehicle across the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: the question mark asks what ground the vehicle will travel over, while the wordplay puts the monarch's cipher inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrain is the land or ground a vehicle crosses.

clue.text: Got decimal wrong in examination

indicators.note: getting something wrong scrambles it, so the letters of decimal are rearranged

explanation.surface: A student misplaced a decimal point in a test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got' and 'in' are links; 'examination' is a physical check-up, not a school test.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical is a physical check-up by a doctor.

clue.text: Once distracted master's making further contributions

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for master, as in MA
adding means putting in more

explanation.surface: A teacher once frazzled keeps chipping in more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' marks the word as archaic, best known from Hardy's 'Far from the Madding Crowd'.
explanation.definitionFit: Madding is an old word for frenzied or acting wildly, as if mad.

clue.text: Plant or stick

parts.note: in heraldry or is the colour gold
a rod is a stick

explanation.surface: Put something in the ground, or a cane instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' looks like a conjunction but is the heraldic word for gold, giving GOLDEN; 'Plant' is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Goldenrod is a tall garden plant with yellow flower spikes.

clue.text: Some popular go-between achieves movement

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A well-liked intermediary manages to get things moving.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'movement', a piece of music; 'achieves' only links, since largo itself does not mean achieving movement.
explanation.definitionFit: A largo is a slow musical movement, named from its tempo marking.

clue.text: A French male gets diminutive Margaret to take in washing?

parts.note: un is the masculine French word for a
Peg is a short form of Margaret

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's Peggy takes in laundry for a living.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' and 'to' are links. 'Take in washing' suggests doing laundry for money, but here it is unpegging clothes from the line.
explanation.definitionFit: To unpeg washing is to remove its clothes pegs and bring it in off the line.

clue.text: Edict of our country to control sea

parts.note: the UK, from the point of view of a British setter

indicators.note: control in the sense of manipulate, so the letters of sea are rearranged

explanation.surface: A national decree to rule the waves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' and 'to' are links; 'control' reworks SEA into ASE.
explanation.definitionFit: A ukase was a decree of the Russian tsar, now any arbitrary order.

clue.text: Great type of beer gets right to the heart

indicators.note: to the heart means the right letter is shifted into the middle of the beer word

parts.note: lager is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A big pint of lager that gets straight to the point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' is a link; R moves from the end of LAGER to its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Large means big, as great does.

clue.text: I am overwhelmed by a country of liveliness

indicators.note: overwhelmed by means the first phrase is surrounded by the country

parts.note: a nation is a country
I am contracts to I'm

explanation.surface: A traveller swamped by a whole nation's spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link; 'overwhelmed by' means the contraction is swallowed by the country word, which follows the 'a' from the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Animation means vivacity, being full of life.

clue.text: Getting out ecologists venues?

parts.note: in cricket, bowling a batsman gets him out
environmentalists are called greens

explanation.surface: Environmentalists being dismissed from their meeting places.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the bowler gets batsmen out; bowling greens are lawns for bowls.
explanation.definitionFit: Bowling greens are the lawns where the game of bowls is played, so places for it.
